# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) open standard for magnetic wireless charging. It tops out at 15W, and a ring of magnets aligns the phone and charger for better efficiency and easier use ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The Verge notes that Qi2 is based on Apple's MagSafe tech, with Apple contributing to the standard ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (technically Qi v2.2.1, also branded **Qi2 25W**) is the newer version. It raises the cap to 25W, nearly 70% more power than Qi2, and the WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first certified products appeared in July 2025 ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program for iPhone. Per Macworld, the differences from plain Qi2 are:
- Certified MagSafe chargers have an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them.
- They also have a magnetometer to prevent compass interference.
- Apple certifies 15W for most iPhones and up to 25W for iPhone 16 and later ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)).

In Macworld's tests, 15W MagSafe and 15W Qi2 chargers charged at about the same speed.

## What this means in practice

| | Max speed | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Uncertified "MagSafe-compatible" | Usually 7.5W | Magnets only, so charging takes about twice as long ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)) |
| Qi2 | 15W | Works with iPhone 12 or later; the iPhone 12 is unofficial per Macworld |
| Qi2.2 / Qi2 25W | 25W | Full speed only on newer phones |
| Apple MagSafe | 15W or 25W | Apple's current charger is also Qi2 25W certified |

- **Your phone sets the limit.** Apple says 25W applies to the iPhone 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max, 17, 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach 22.5W, the iPhone Air 20W, and the iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)). The iPhone 16e has no MagSafe or Qi2 magnets.
- **The charger's power adapter matters.** Apple recommends a 30W or higher USB-C adapter for 25W charging.
- **Android support is thin.** Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W, and the Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 series is "Qi2 Ready," meaning it needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## Which to buy

For an iPhone, any Qi2 or Qi2.2 charger works magnetically. Pick Qi2.2 only if you have a 16-series or newer iPhone and want the fastest speed. Check the WPC logo or its [certified product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/) to avoid uncertified 7.5W chargers.

If you want a safe default, [Apple's MagSafe Charger (2 m, $49)](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8) is certified for Qi2 25W and also comes in a 1 m length. Macworld lists the 1 m version at $39. The charger doesn't include a power adapter.

If you tell me your phone model and whether you want a pad, stand or power bank, I can narrow it down.
